idiom_name: page builder + one renderer per channel, joined by an explicit logical page
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: two stages with an explicit artefact between them. Stage one is a page builder that reads the domain data and emits a logical page - a tree of page elements (sections, fields, collections) named with domain vocabulary and carrying no channel-specific markup, escaping or display formatting. Stage two is one renderer per output channel: it walks (or transforms) the logical page and produces the channel's bytes, owning all formatting, escaping and layout decisions. Keep the page vocabulary explicit and versioned, keep renderers read-only with respect to the domain layer, and select the renderer by content negotiation or an explicit format at the boundary. The logical page is also the test seam: it can be asserted, cached and logged without parsing markup. Collapse the two stages only when a single channel exists.
code_sketch:
page  = build_page(domain_data)          # stage 1: logical page, no markup
html  = render_html(page)                # stage 2: one renderer per channel
print = render_pdf(page)
feed  = render_json(page)
# renderer = resolver.channel(request)   # content negotiation, not page logic
pitfalls: Letting the logical page carry channel-specific attributes or pre-escaped text defeats the split and breaks the next renderer.
Renderers that query the domain layer turn the second stage into a hidden third one and couple presentation to persistence.
Defining a different logical page per channel that ignores the vocabulary the other renderers use.

Wrong move: chaining two XSLT stages inside one XSLT 1.0 processor -> the stage-one result is a result tree fragment that stage two cannot re-parse, so the pipeline silently flattens to text or fails -> serialise the logical page explicitly between stages (or use an XSLT 2.0/3.0 processor such as Saxon, where intermediate results can be pipelined).

Wrong move: naming a content-template-plus-layout-wrapper 'Two Step View' (the Aura.View-style shortcut) -> the intermediate is pre-rendered markup, so a second channel still needs its own copy of stage one -> only call it a logical page if stage two could not tell HTML from PDF by reading it.
